Package for jobless farmers in Assam 
*84. SHRI URKHAO GWRA BRAHMA: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the fact that due to heavy flood every year, small 
and marginal farmers in Assam are suffering serious economic setbacks and the number of 
such farmers is huge; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that number of jobless farmers is increasing every year, resulting 
in steep decline in agriculture/foodgrain production; and 
(c) if so, whether Government have a ny scheme to extend financial package for the 
hapless farmers? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a) to (c) A statement is 
laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (c) Government is aware that the farmers of Assam are adversely affected by flood 
causing setback to the agricultural production of the State. In such a situation, the State 
Governments provide various services to the affected farmers including the required relief to 
them in the event of failure or destruction of crops. Government of India, also supports and 
supplements the efforts of the State Government through various schemes, programmes 
along with financial and other supports. Funds are available with the State Government under 
the Calamity Relief Fund for taking up nece ssary relief measures in the wake of natural 
calamities including flood. Government of India and State Governments contribute to these 
funds in the ratio of 3:1. Additional assistance over and above the Calamity Relief Fund is 
considered by the Government of India from the National Calamity Contingency Fund in 
accordance with the established procedures and norms. 
2. As per the report received from the State Government, the number of farm families 
affected by floods during 2007-08 is about 10.04 lakh covering an area of about 4.11 lakh 
hectares. National Sample Survey Report on Employment and Unemployment situation in India 
indicates that in Assam of about 74.3% of employed persons in rural areas are in agriculture in 
2004-05 against the corresponding figure of 67.7% during 1999- 2000 and 79.2% during 
1993-94. Thus, employments in agriculture shows a fluctuating trend. 
3. From the available information it is observed that food grain production in Assam has 
shown a declining trend due to climatic aberrations in the recent past. The data of last 5 
years is given below.

(a) Since procurement of foodgrains under Minimum Support Price (MSP)

* 85. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMIL Y 
WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there is any proposal under conside ration of Government to allow the 
Ayurvedic Yoga, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy (AYUSH) doctors to 
use the life saving drugs in emergency which are normally prescribed by the Allopathic 
doctors;  
(b) whether any demand in this regard has so far be en made by the AYUSH 
Medical Society; and 

24      Written answers to [RAJYA SABHA] Slurred questions 
(c) if so, what is the reaction of Government thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBUMANI RAMA 
DOSS): (a) to (c) The matter regarding  qualified practitioners of Ayurveda, Unani, 
Siddha and Homoeopathy systems prescribing allopathic medicines has been examined 
in depth by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal No.89 of 1987 Dr. 
Mukhtiar Chand and others versus State of Punjab  and others. Representations have 
been received from time to time on this matter and accordingly Department of AYUSH 
entrusted the study of the contemporary acts on medical practice in the light of 
judgement of Hon'ble Supreme Court in 1987 Dr. Mukhtiar Ch and and others versus 
State of Punjab and others and other similar judgements. Drugs can be sold and supplied 
by a Pharmacist or a Druggist only on a prescription of a Registered Medical 
Practitioner and who can also store them for, treatment of patients. 
According to Section 2 (e) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1995, Registered 
Medical Practitioner means a person- 
(i) holding a qualification granted by an authority specified or notified under Section 
3 of the Indian Medical Degrees Act, 1916 (7 of 1916) , or specified in the 
Schedules to the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 (102 of 1956); or 
(ii) registered or eligible for registration in a medical register of a State meant for the 
registration of persons practicing the modern scientific system of medicin e 
(excluding the Homoeopathy system of medicine); or 
(iii) registered in a medical register (other than a register for the registration of 
Homoeopathic practitioners) of a State, who although not falling within sub -
clause (i) or sub -clause (ii)  is declared by a general or special order made by 
the State Government in this  behalf as a person practicing the modern 
scientific system of medicine for the purposes of this Act. 
Hon'ble Supreme Court upheld the validity of Rule 2 (ee) (iii)  as well as the 
notifications issued by various State Governments thereunder allowing Ayurveda, 
Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy practitioners to prescribe allopathic medicines.  
In view of the above judgement, Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy 
practitioners can prescribe allopathic medicines under Rule 2 (ee) (iii)  only in those 
States where they are authorized to do so by a general or special order made by the 
concerned State Government in that regard. Practitioners of Indian Medicine holding 
the degrees in integrated courses can also prescribe allopathic medicines if any State act 
in the State in which they are practicing recognizes their qualification as sufficient for 
registration in the State Medical Register.

(c) whether such steps would keep large number of deserving sections out of the

decision; and 
(e) if so, the details of the steps taken by Government? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a) to (e) The Planning Commission is the nodal agency in 
the Government of India for estimation of poverty in the country. The Commission 
estimates poverty across all the States by followi ng a uniform methodology and 
releases the poverty estimates from time to time. When TPDS was introduced in 1997, 
the poverty estimates released by the Planning Commission for the year 1993 -94 were 
available. According to those estimates, percentage of popu lation below poverty line 
was 36%. Population estimates made by the Registrar General and Census 
Commissioner for 1995 were also available at that time. The Government decided to 
use poverty estimates of the Planning Commission for the year 1993 -94 and population 
estimates of 1995 for working out the number of BPL households in the country for the 
purpose of making allocations of foodgrains under the TPDS. This number of 
households was 5.96 crores. 
Subsequently, in November, 2000, the Government decided to use the population 
estimates of 1st March, 2000 instead of 1995 for working out the number of BPL 
households in the country for the purpose of TPDS allocations. The number of BPL 
households in the country worked out on this basis is 6.52 crores. The Govern ment has 
continued to use this number of BPL households for the allocations. 
In March, 2007, the Planning Commission has released poverty estimates for 2004-
05 which are comparable with the poverty estimates of 1993 -04. According to these 
estimates, in the  country as a whole the percentage of population below poverty line 
was 27.5%. 
The Government has received requests from some State Governments for accepting 
higher number of BPL households for allocation of foodgrains. However, the 
Government has continue d to use the number of BPL households worked out on the 
basis of poverty estimates of 1993- 94 projected on the population estimate of March, 
2000.

†*91. PROF. RAM DEO BHANDARY: 
SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: 
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:  
(a) whether information has been received regarding availability of big quantity of 
fake medicines in many States of the country; 
(b) if so, the details of raids, recovered fake medicines, registered cases and arrests 
made during the last six months* State-wise;

Written answers to [17 AUG., 2007] Starred questions    31 
(c) whether Government intend to make present law against criminals engaged in 
the business of fake medicines more stringent; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBUMANI RAMA 
DOSS): (a) to (d) There have been some reports of spurious drugs from some places  
of the country which are being investigated by  State Drugs Control and Central  
Drugs Control Administration. Allegedly counterfeit/fake medicines were recovered  
by the U.P. Drug Control Authorities along with Police from some parts of U.P. like  
Muzzafarnagar, Ghaziabad, Meerut, Agra, Modinagar, etc. S imiarly, in Bolangir distrct  
in Orissa, fake medicines were detected. Reports are given In the. Statement -I and II 
(See below).  
Data Pertaining to 2004 -05,2005-06, 2006-07 are given in Statements at III, IV and 
V (c) respectively (See below). Last 6 months data is being collected from the States. 
The Government is proposing to, amend the Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940, to 
provide for stringent punishment to the offenders wherein a maximum penalty of life 
imprisonment and a fine upto rupees ten lakhs has been provided and provision of 
special courts for speedy trial of drug related offences and making all such offences 
cognizable and non-bailable. The Bill is likely to be introduced in the present Monsoon 
Session of Parliament. 
Statement-I 
Action Taken by U.P Government 
The following action has been taken by the Uttar Pradesh Government after 
disclosure in the electronic and print media regarding manufacture and sale of 
counterfeit drugs: 
1. An order had been passed on 4.06.2007 to carry out drive against 
manufacture and sale of sub -standard, spurious, and misbranded drugs. 
Further, all Commissioners and District Magistrate have been strictly 
instructed to carry out drives against spurious/counterfeit drugs by orders of 
the Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary both dated 31.07.2007. This drive 
will be conducted till 30th September, 2007 and will be carried out by the 
health department alongwith Police and officials of the other departments. 
Instruction have already been issued to take strict action against 
manufacturers and dealer of sub-standard and spurious drugs under the Drugs 
& Cosmetic Act and Rules and the IPC. 
2. Between 20.07.2007 and 2.08.2007 raids were carried out in the Districts of 
Meerut, Bahraich, Lucknow, J.P. Nagar, Bijnor, Bulandshahar, Faizabad, 
Rampur, Moradabad, Agra, Muzzafarnagar, Sultanpur, Ghaziabad and 
Saharanpur. During the drive, 122 sales premises were raided and 238 
samples were drawn 10 FIR were filed and 17 persons arrested. 
3. Grant of all new Wholesale and Retail Licences in the State of  U.P. have 
been suspended by an order dated 24.07.2007, till further order. 
4. The Drugs Controller of UP and the Drugs Inspector of Meerut have been 
suspended and necessary disciplinary actions have been started against them.

Corruption in PDS 
†*92. SHRI SURENDRA LATH: Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD 
AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fa ct that foodgrains allocated under the Public Distribution 
System are not reaching the lower strata of people and the poor and major part of the 
same is directly reaching open market at high prices through black market;  
(b) whether Government are aware that mo st of the foodgrains under this scheme is 
going to big companies; 
(c) whether Government are contemplating any new scheme for preventing this 
corruption prevalent in PDS; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; 
. (e) whether it is a fact- that PDS has completely failed in the country and only 
middlemen and big corhpanies are its beneficiaries; and 
(f)     if so, action taken by Government in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a) to (f) TPDS is operated unde r the joint responsibility of 
Government of India and State/UT Governments. The Government of India carries out 
procurement of foodgrains for the TPDS, their storage, transportation and allocation to 
the State/UT Governments. The responsibility for allocation of foodgrains within the 
State, identification of eligible  families and issuance of ration cards to them, and 
supervision of distribution of allocated foodgrains to eligible families through the fair 
price shops rests with the  State/UT Governments. 
The State/UT Governments are mandated to ensure that the foodgrains allocated 
under the TPDS reach the targeted families and no leakages/diversions take place.  
Details of offtake of foodgrains (rice and wheat) under TPDS against the allocations 
made to State/UT Governments during the last five years are given below.

These details of  foodgrains lifted by the State/UT Governments indicate an 
increasing trend and a larger coverage. 
However, there have been complaints about shortcomings in TPDS. So for 
independent feedback, the Targeted Public Distribution System was got evaluated by

New Delhi.

Their reports received in year 2005 reported that ther e were diversions/leakages of 
foodgrains, inclusion and exclusion errors in identifying targeted beneficiaries and 
operations of Fair Price Shops (FPSs) were not financially viable. 
Therefore, to strengthen the TPDS, including curbing of leakages and diver sion, 
though no new scheme has been introduced by the Government, a nine -point action plan 
was formulated in 2006. This is being implemented by States/UT Governments. Its 
implementation is being monitored by the Central Government. Required action is being

Following strategies are being implemented for Malaria and Chikungunya: 
MALARIA 
I.    Disease Management 
• Early case detection and complete treatment. 
• Strengthening of referral services 
• Epidemic preparedness and rapid response 
II. Integrated Vector Management for reducing mosquitoes' density 
• Indoor Residual Spraying in selected high risk areas 
• Use of Insecticide treated bed nets 
• Use of Larvivorous fishes. 
• Anti larval measures in urban areas including biolarvicides 
• Minor environmental engineering 
III. Supporting Interventions: 
• Behaviour Change Communication 
• Public Private Partnership & Inter-sectoral convergence 
• Human Resource Development through capacity building 
• Operational  research   including   studies  on  drug  resistance  and 
insecticide susceptibility 
The States in eastern parts in the country have also been provided enhanced support 
through Global Funds to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (GFATM) and World 
Bank. The supports includes insecticide treated bed -nets to Vulnerable groups, Rapid 
diagnostic kits, treatment of P. falciparum cases with Artesunate

early diagnosis and treatment of malaria cases. Capacity building and BCC components

CHIKUNGUNYA 
• There is no vaccine or specific medicine available against Chikungunya 
infection. Vector control is thus very important in controlling or preventing 
transmission of Chikungunya. 
• Government of India has prepared a long Term Action Plan for prevention 
and control of Chikungunya and sent to the States for implementation along 
with detailed guidelines. 
• Central Teams from the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare visited the 
affected States to review the situation and provide, technical guidance and 
Chikungunya situation is being continuously monitored.

affected States for social mobilization of community for Source reduction 
and purchase of additional insecticides/larvicides for prevention and control 
of Chikungunya in the States.

NAP stress on some crops 
†595. SHRI LALIT KISHORE CHATUR VEDI: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that in the National Agriculture Policy all stress has been  
laid on some crops like wheat, rice, co tton, sugarcane and ground nut and no  
attention has been given to eco-friendly crops in the country; and 
(b) the schemes formulated or under consideration for development of good  
quality seeds of these local crops, their publicity, storage and distribution? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI KANTI 
LAL BHUR1A): (a) The National Agriculture Policy envisages at a sustainable growth 
in excess of 4% per annum in the agriculture sector through efficient use of resources 
and conservation of  soil, water and bio -diversity. Balanced and conjunctive use of bio -
mass, organic and inorganic fertilizers and controlled use of agro chemicals through 
integrated nutrients and pest management are being promoted to achieve the sustainable 
growth in agriculture sector. The country is bestowed with diverse agro -climatic 
conditions favourable for the cultivation of diverse crops like foodgrains crops, 
commercial crops, horticulture, plantation, spices, trees, etc. and accordingly, 
schemes/programmes are formu lated. To promote crop diversification from cereal to 
non-cereal crops, an Integrated Scheme of Oilseeds, Pulses. Oil Palm and Maize 
(ISOPOM) is being implemented since 2004. National Horticulture Mission is being 
implemented since the year 2005 for ensuri ng end to end approach with backward and 
forward linkages covering research, post harvest management, processing and 
marketing. A new centrally- sponsored Scheme the National Bamboo Mission, was 
approved during 2006 to bring in additional area under bamboo in the forest and non-
forest area. To encourage eco -friendly crops, a National Project on Organic farming has 
also been taken up for production, promotion, certification and development of organic 
farming in the country. 
(b) Government has made concerted efforts to make quality seeds available to the 
farmers. In this connection a National Seeds Plan has been prepared for all major crops 
including a seed production system to form a continuous chain within the cycle. A 
Central sector scheme titled as Developm ent and Strengthening of Infrastructure 
Facilities for Production and Distribution of Quality Seeds is being implemented with 
the components, namely (i) Transport Subsidy on Movement of Seeds; (ii) 
Establishment and Maintenance of Seed Bank; (iii)  Quality Control Arrangement on 
Seeds—National Seeds Research and Training Centre, Varanasi; (iv) Seed Village 
Scheme; (v) Assistance for Creation of Infrastructure Facilities in Public Sector; (vi) 
Assistance for Boosting Seed Production in Private Sector; (vii)  Human Resource 
Development; (viii)  Assistance for Seed Export; (ix) Use of Biotechnology in 
Agriculture; and (x) Promoting Hybrid Seeds.

Statement 
Measures taken to prevent the spread of the disease 
The following measures were taken in Manipur to prevent the spread of Avian 
Influenza: 
1. Demarcation of infected and surveillance areas was carried out  in accordance 
with the Action Plan. An area of 0 -5 kms. was designated as the Infected Zone 
and a further area of 5-10 kms. was designated as the Surveillance Zone. 
 

Written answers to [17 AUG.. 2007] Unstarred questions     57 
2. The poultry, both backyard and commercial, has been culled in a radius of 0 -5 
kms around the affected farm premises. 
3. Other infected materials such as poultry eggs, feathers, feed, feed materials, 
protective cloth used -by the staff engaged in operations etc. has also been 
destroyed. Approximately 25,242 kg of feed material and 28 thousand eggs have 
been destroyed. 
4. Thereafter cleaning and disinfection of the infected premises/area has been 
undertaken, which is under progress. 
5. Physical surveillance in the 5 -10 km area is being continued to ascertain if there 
is any further unusual mortality. No unusual mortality has been reported in the 
surveillance zone as well as from anywhere else in the State. 
6. The Government of India has maintained strategic reserve of poultry vaccines. 
The option of vaccination is thus available to the country. However, vaccination 
has not yet been introduced in the country. 
7. The personnel involved in containment work were provided personal protective 
equipment and brought under cover of Tamiflu by the health authorities. 
8. It is the policy of the Government of India to pay compensation to owner for 
culled poultry. The costs are being shared on a 50:50 basis with the State 
Government. Approximately 75 lakhs Indian Rupees have been paid as 
compensation. 
Moreover, the following measures have also been taken up by the Government 
of India to prevent spread of the disease to other States: 
1. Action Plan for Preparedness, Control and Containment of Avian Influenza for 
Animal Husbandry has been prepared and circulated by Governmen t of India to 
facilitate action by the State Governments. 
2. Import of poultry & poultry products has been banned completely from Avian 
Influenza positive countries. 
3. All the State Governments have been alerted to be vigilant about the outbreak of 
the disease if any. 
4. Border security formations and custom field formations have been alerted. 
5. State of the north -east specially those bordering outbreak countries like 
Bangladesh, Myanmar and China have been alerted. 
6. Nationwide surveillance is continuing. Approximatel y 1,43,000 samples have 
been tested at High Security Animal Disease Laboratory (HSADL), Bhopal since 
February 2006. 
7. Testing for Avian Influenza have also been started at Regional Level viz., 
Regional Disease Diagnostic Laboratories, Kolkata, Bangalore, Pun e and 
Jallandhar. So far, approximately 37,000 samples have been tested in the 
regional laboratories.

8. The training of veterinary personnel in preparedness, control and containment 
started in O ctober 2005 at regional level is continuing. The training was shifted 
to State level basis by the Government of India from September 2006. More than 
30% of the veterinary workforce under employment of Government has been 
trained as Master-Trainers for further field trainings. 
9. A National workshop on Preparedness, Control and Containment of Avian 
Influenza was organized at Pune during May, 2007 and recently a Regional 
Workshop of the North -Eastern States (Sikkim, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, 
Manipur, Mizoram, A runachal Pradesh, Nagaland and West Bengal) was

improved/hybrid production technology, integrated pest management, transfer of 
technology, farm implements, installation of sprinkler irrigation system, varietal 
replacement and production of certified seeds.

and Maize" (ISOPOM) is in place since 01.04.2004 to increase the productivity and 
production of these crops. Under this scheme, assistance is provid ed on 75:25 basis 
between the Government of India and the State Governments for production of 
breeder/foundation/certified seeds, crash programme for quality seed procruction, 
distribution of certified seed, and Minikits, infrastructure development and integrated 
pest management.

varieties are made available to growers, inter cropping of sugarcane has been  
developed to provide mid- term income to sugarcane growers, trash mulching and  
drought management technology have been developed for management of moisture  
stress, bioagents have been mass multiplied and released for biocontrol of woolly  
aphid. - 
For cotton, a scheme is under implementation in 13 States to increase production 
and productivity of cotton by focusing on increasing availability of cotton seeds,

limit in 12 calendar months from 20 per cent to 10 per cent for more effective check on

625. SHRI PRASANTA CHATTERJEE:  
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:

Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether an in principle decision has been taken by Government to revive the 
eight closed urea producing units of Hindustan Fertilizer Corporation (HFC) and 
Fertilizers Corporation of India (FCI) with natural gas as feed stock; 
(b) if so, the detail thereof, plant -wise and the companies entrusted to handle the 
revival of the plants; 
(c) wherefrom the feedstock natural gas would be sourced and by when the laying 
of gas pipe lines to the plant heads would be completed; and 
(d) the estimated  cost of revival of the above plants and the details of investment 
pattern thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS (SHRI B.K. HANDIQUE): (a) to (d) The Government has decided 'in 
principle' to examine the possibility of revival of closed fertilizer plants of Fertilizer 
Corporation of India Limited (FCIL) and Hindustan Fertilizer Corporation Limited 
(HFCL) subject to the confirmed availability of gas. The decision of the Government 
has been intimated to FCIL and HFCL for implementation. Fertilizer PSUs/Cooperative -
Rashtriya Chemicals and Fertilizers Ltd. (RCF), National Fertilizers Limited (NFL) and 
Krishak Bharati Cooperative Ltd. (KRIBHCO) have shown their intention to participate 
in the revival process of certain units of FCIL and HFCL. Revival of HFCL-Barauni and 
FCIL-Ramagundam through NFL, FCIL -Talcher and HFCL -Durgapur through RCF 
and FCIL-Gorakhpur through KRIBHCO has been proposed. The process of preparing 
techno-economic feasibility reports has been initiated. As regards revival of FCIL -
Korba and Sindri and HFCL-Haldia, options are being explored. 
The gas availability in the country is projected to improve from 2009- 10 onwards. 
The companies are exploring the assured availability of gas for revival of these closed 
units. However, no assured availability of gas has been confirmed yet. 
The pipeline to the plant heads are expected to be drawn as spur lines from the 
projected extension of HBJ Pipeline from Jagdishpur to Haldia for Gorakhpur, 
Durgapur and Barauni units. For Ramagundam, a spur line from the projected Kakinada 
to Uran Gas Pipeline of Reliance" will provide the requisite connectivity. Talcher unit 
is expected to be revived through coal gasification route. However, the connectivity to 
spur line will be initiated only after availability of gas for the project is tied up. 
The estimated cost of revival of the above plants cannot be anticipated at this stage 
owing to several factors such as finalization of production capacity, infrastructural 
requirements etc. However, it is estimated that a one million tonne production capacity 
plant of urea will cost approximately Rs. 3500 crore.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) In 2007, Polio cases have been 
reported from Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Gujarat, Haryana, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar

Written answers to [17 AUG., 2007] Unstarred questions   107 
(c) Yes, Sir. 
(d) Prior to 2006, there was an outbreak in 2002 when 1600 cases of polio were 
detected. The four year cycle is due to accumulation of susceptible children during this 
period. The polio virus survived in Western U.P. and Bihar during the period between 
2002 and 2006 and got enough susceptible children in 2006 to start another outbreak. 
The polio virus survived in Moradabad and JP Nagar due to environmental factors such 
as h igh population density, poor sanitation, high incidence of diarrhoea that' require 
more doses of polio vaccine to be given to children in these areas compared to other 
areas of the country. However, since the overall immunization status of children in 2006  
was much better than what it was in 2002, the number of polio cases seen in 2006 was 
only 676 (compared to 1600 in 2002). The polio outbreak in 2006 started from two 
districts of West U.P.—Moradabad and JP Nagar, from where it spread to other districts 
in West U.P., districts of Central and Eastern U.P., Bihar and other States. 
(e) The Government has taken the following steps to check the polio cases: 
 
(a) Two nationwide polio immunisation campaigns were conducted in January 
and February 2007. These were followed by additional sub -national 
immunisation rounds in the high risk States in March, April, May, July and 
August, 2007. Additional sub- national immunisation rounds are planned 
for September, October and December, 2007. 
(b) The endemic districts of Uttar Pradesh an d Bihar have had more, 
immunisation rounds in the first six  months of 2007 compared to what 
was done during the corresponding period of 2006. 
(c) The mono -valent vaccines have been used extensively in the high risk 
States/areas during 2007 polio immunisation drives. The mono -valent 
vaccines have better efficacy than the tri-valent vaccines used earlier. 
(d) The Government of UP has filled large number of vacant medical officer 
positions to strengthen programme management at the block level. 
(e) There has been a thrust on involving ASHA workers as vaccinators and 
mobilisers in the high risk areas to ensure better reach of the polio 
immunisation drives. 
(f) Emphasis has been on reducing the missed children in the high risk areas 
of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar by ensuring re -visits of vaccination teams to 
houses where children get missed during the first attempt by vaccination 
teams. 
- 
(g) All new- borns are being identified, vaccinated and tracked for polio 
vaccination during the polio immunisation drives. 
(h) Migratory population from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar in other States like 
Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat, West Bengal are being covered every time there 
is a polio drive in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. 
(i) Efforts are being made to improve sanitation in the highest risk areas of Uttar 
Pradesh and Bihar through the involvement of Ministry of Rural 
Development.

cornea, etc. in the country;

Separation of medical education and research 
663. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) the aims and objectives  of the proposed separate departments of medical 
research and education; 
(b) what are the reasons for creating a separate medical research department when 
there is Indian Council of Medical Research which is already looking after medical 
research; 
(c) whether the proposed department is on the recommendations of the Scientific 
Advisory Committee of the Prime Minister; 
(d) whether the proposed department is on the lines of Department of Scientific and 
Industrial Research; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF S TATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) The aims and objectives are to 
deal and encourage fundamental -  the 'blue Sky' research for generation and 
advancement of knowledge; strategic research - aimed at developmen t of better or new 
tools (diagnostics, drugs, vaccines, devices etc.); clinical research -  testing the new tools 
developed; and operational research - assessing the efficiency of the tools under 
field/programme condition; encourage harnessing of new knowle dge of gene and gene 
functions, expand capacity for structural biology in the health sector, particularly 
making the health sector utilize fruits of the research; promote clinical research and 
speedy translation of research results into products. 
(b) Given the complexities of current and future health challenges and  
opportunities provided by modern biology, no single agency is likely to address  
these effectively. There is an urgent need for a new Department to steer and  
coordinate health research activities  in the country. To convert the above vision into  
concrete action, an exclusive Department headed by a Secretary is required only to  
deal with health research and ICMR will continue to be a Society under the proposed  
department 
(c) The topic was examined by th e Scientific Advisory Committee of the Prime 
Minister and recommended for implementation. 
(d) and (e) The proposed Department would be an independent new Department 
within the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. It would facilitate the proper 
coordination between other scientific departments and provide the necessary impetus to 
medical research. The ICMR would function as an autonomous organization in the 
proposed Department for Health Research. Like in the two Councils (CSIR and ICAR), 
the DG, ICMR will also be the Secretary of the proposed Department.

Statement 
The Salient features of the HIV/AIDS Bill 2007 
The main objectives of the legislation are to prevent and control the spread of 
HIV/AIDS and protect the rights of those infected and affected by HIV/AIDS. The main 
chapters of the law include: 
(i) Prohibition of discrimination related to HIV/AIDS within th e public and 
private spheres. This chapter addresses discrimination in employment, 
education, healthcare, travel, residence, accommodation, insurance etc. It 
also addresses the issue of hate and discriminatory speech in the HIV 
context. 
(ii) Requirement of  informed consent for HIV -related testing, HIV -related 
treatment and HIV -related research. This chapter statutorises existing 
standards of informed consent and the exceptions to it. 
(iii) Guarantee of confidentiality of HIV -related information (including H IV+ 
status) and exceptions to it. 
(iv) The right to access treatment related to HIV/AIDS as part of the right to 
health recognized under the Indian Constitution and the International 
Covenant on Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights to which India is a 
signatory. The chapter provides for access to comprehensive HIV - related 
treatment including diagnostics, ARVs, nutritional supplements etc. 
(v) The right to a safe working environment for health care workers and other 
persons whose occupation may put them at risk of exposure to HIV. 
(vi) Protection of strategies for risk reduction, which are otherwise subject to 
criminal sanction under various laws that have severely impeded risk 
reduction work with sex workers, injecting drug users and men who have 
sex with men in the past. 
(vii) Norms for Information, Education and Communication programmes and 
materials.

(viii) The creation of innovative implementation mechanisms including 
institutional grievance  redressal machinery, Health Ombudspersons and 
HIV/AIDS Authorities. This will  be supported by Special Procedures to 
be followed in courts, including suppression of identity, speedy trials 
and proceedings etc. 
(ix) Special provisions for those who are disproportionately affected by the 
epidemic, particularly women, children and young persons and persons in 
the care and custody of the State who due to social, economic, legal and 
other factors find themselves more vulnerable to HIV.

Population control 
670. SHRI DHARAM PAL SABHARWAL: 
SHRI M.V MYSURA REDDY: 
Will the MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:  
(a) whether Government proposed to fix any time bound schedule for Family 
welfare programmes; 
(b) if so, the details in this regard; 
(c) whether Government propose to implement the policy on population  control in a 
systematic and uniform manner; and 
(d) if so, what are the programmes of Government on population control and what is 
the amount earmarked for the same for the next two years? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) to (d) India is the first country 
in the world to start the National Family Welfare Programme in 1952 with the objective 
of reducing the birth rate to the extent necessary to stabilize the population at a level 
consistent with  the requirement of the national: economy. In, keeping with the 
democratic tradition of the country, the Family Welfare programme seeks to promote 
responsible and Planned Parenthood through voluntary and informed choice of family 
planning methods best suited to individual acceptors. 
The National Population Policy, 2000 adopted in Feb. 2000, provides a policy 
framework for advancing goals and prioritising strategies to meet the reproductive and 
child health needs of the people and to achieve net replacement level i.e. Total Fertility 
Rate (TFR) of 2.1 by 2010. It is based upon the need to simultaneously address issues of 
child survival, maternal health and contraception, while increasing outreach and 
coverage of a comprehensive package of reproductive and chi ld health services with 
government, industry and the voluntary non-government sector, working in partnership. 
To carry forward the above objective of National Family Welfare Programme the 
first phase of the Reproductive and Child Health Programme (RCH) programme was in 
operation since 1997. The second phase i.e. RCH-II programme has commenced from 
April, 2005 for a period of 5 years. The main objective of RCH -II is to bring about a 
change in the three critical health indicators viz. Total Fertility Rate (TF R), Infant 
Mortality Rate (IMR) and Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) consistent with the goal 
enshrined in the National Population Policy 2000. 
The Government has launched National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) on 12th 
April, 2005 for providing integrated comprehensive Primary Healthcare Services, 
especially to the poor and vulnerable sections of the society throughout the country. The 
NRHM also aims to provide overarching umbrella to the existing programmes of Health 
and Family Welfare including RCH-II. 
Population stabilization, gender and demographic balance are some of the objectives 
of NRHM. It provides a thrust for reduction of child and maternal mortality 

Written answers to [17 AUG, 2007] Unstarred- questions   133 
and reduces the fertility rates. The Mis sion further seeks to build greater ownership of 
the programme among the community through involvement of Panchayati Raj 
Institutions, NGOs and other stake holders at National, State, District and Sub -District 
levels to achieve the goals of National Popula tion Policy 2000 and National Health 
Policy. 
The approved outlay for the NRHM for the year 2007- 08 is Rs.11010 crore and 
projected requirement of funds during 2008- 09 is Rs. 17290 crore. Funding requirement 
for population stabilisation activities of the re spective, states will also be met out of the 
above outlay.

blood donation camps annually.

Council and oversee the implementation of various activities 
   to ensure access of quality blood to needy patients.

Kidney problem in Goa 
675. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Ministe r of HEALTH AND  
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that residents of Canacona Taluka, specially those living 
along the coastal and hilly areas in Goa suffer from mysterious kidney problems which 
has remained un-diagnosed for the last several years; 
(b) whether the State of Goa has ever requested the Central Government to help 
them in diagnosing the problem; 
(c) whether any Central agency has visited the Taluka for the purpose; and 
(d) the details of the report, Government have obtained, if any, fr om the said 
agency? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) to (d) According to Indian 
Council of Medical Research, New Delhi the high prevalence of Kidney diseases in 
Canacona Taluka of Goa has b een a matter of concern for the local people for the last 
several years. The Epidemiological Cell, Directorate of Health Services, Government of 
Goa approached the Council's National Institute of Occupational Health, Meghaninagar, 
Ahmedabad. The NIOH team visited Goa and carried out Environmental cum Biological 
monitoring in February, 2005. It observed that clinically the disease seems to be similar 
to Balkan Endemic Nephropathy (BEN) which is an environmentally acquired disease, 
possibly caused by mycotoxi n produced by fungi in mouldy cereals and food 
commodities; and aromatic compounds present in the drinking water. Further conclusion 
can only be drawn by correlating the clinical picture biotechnical investigation of blood 
and urine and other pathological investigations and its correlation with environmental 
factors. 
Vaccine for cholera 
676. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Scientists in the University of Tokyo have developed a 
vaccine from rice to cure cholera disease; 
(b) if so, the details thereof;. 
(c) whether the requisite quality of rice is available in India; 
(d) if so, whether Government will take clue from the scientists from Tokyo to 
indigenously develop the vaccine; and 
(e) the anticipated cost of new vaccine as compared to traditional one? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) and (b) According to Indian  

Written answers to [17 AUG, 2007] Unstarred questions   137 
Council of Medical Research (ICMR) a team of Japanese Researcher Hiroshi Kiyono at 
Tokyo University found a way of genetically engineering a strain of rice. It contains a 
vaccine against cholera capable of inducing antigen specific immune responses in both 
systemic and mucosa compartments without the use of syringe and needle. The work is 
preliminary having been tested only in mice. As per researches more basic studies are 
needed to test the vaccine in a primate. 
(c) The rice- based cholera vaccine was created by i nserting the genetic material .  
from the cholera bacterium into the sequenced genome of the rice plant. The 
researchers used two types of rice plants to generate the vaccine: Kitaake, which  
produces normal rice, and Hosetsu, which produces warf -type rice. The rice plant  
Oryza sativa is a common species in India also. The rice plants would also have to  
be grown under carefully controlled conditions to ensure appropriate vaccine 
production. 
 
(d) It will depend on successful clinical trials of the Vaccine.  
(e) It is anticipated that the initial costs of genetically engineering rice to produce a 
cholera vaccine will be nominally high but on a per dose basis the cost would be very 
very low. The vaccine will not require refrigeration, nor a needle.

685. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY

(a) whether Government are aware that in India 65 per cent of births are caesarean

deaths are due to anaesthesia related complications occurring during caesareans 
deliveries; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY

the total deliveries, 7.1 % were by Caesarian Section, which is within the WHO norm of 
5-15%. 
There is no data to indicate that 52% of maternal deaths are due to anesthesia related 
complications occurring during caesarian deliveries. As per the latest survey reports 
published by the Office of RG I (SRS -  2001-03), the causes of Maternal Deaths in the 
country are - Hemorrhage - 38%, Sepsis - 11%, Abortion - 8%, Obstructed Labour -

Conditions" also includes deaths due to anesthesia related complications during labour 
and delivery.

of the total caesarian section deliveries, 65.4% were conducted in private institutions

t694. SHRI SATYAVRAT CHATURVEDI: 
SHRI MOTILAL VORA: 
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether as per a research fin ding in America, two medicines meant for diabetes 
are the cause of heart disease; 
(b) whether Government would conduct investigation in this regard; 
(c) if so, by when the results of such investigation would be received; 
 
(d) whether Government would impose ban on the use of these two medicines till 
the results of the investigations are received; and    . 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI ANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) to (e) A research was carried out 
by Dr. Steven Nissen of the Cleveland Clinic in the US by conducting meta analysis of 
42 trial results of only one anti -diabetic drug Rosiglitazone. In the recent article 
published in New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM), the results of meta analysis 
claimed that Resiglitazone is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disorders. 
However, in the opinion of another scientific journal Lancet, it was reported that to 
avoid unnecessary panic, a calmer and more considered approach to the safety of 
Rosiglitazone is needed. The Scientific Advisory Committee of US FDA has examined 
the issue and clear decision has come out of the committee. Out of 23 members of the 
committee, 22 recommended for the continued use of the drug. The US FDA takes 
decisions based on the recommendations of Scientific Advisory Committee. 
In view of above, Rosiglitazone is being brought under focused monitoring of 
adverse drug reactions in the National Pharmacovigilance Programme.

Expert committee on the status of private caterers 
698. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the findings of the expert committee on the status of private caterers serving in 
the Railways; 
(b) what were the terms of reference of the committee; 
(c) whether Government agree with the committee's observation about unhygienic 
conditions in which such catering facilities are kept; 
(d) if so, what steps have been taken against such erring caterers; 

Written answers to [17 AUG., 2007] Unstarred questions   165 
(e) whether Government agree with the recommendations of the expert committee; 
if so, the details thereof; and 
(f) by when such recommendations would be implemented? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI R. VELU): 
(a) to (f) No 'Expert Committee' as such has been set up by Railways to look into the 
status of private caterers of Indian Railways. However, Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the 
context of a Public Interest Litigation have constituted a committee, who have observed 
as under:- 
1. Every kitchen should have a complete and proper team of qualified staff 
trained in running and ma intaining a kitchen and undertaking cooking 
operations. 
2. There should be properly qualified and expert consultants on board of 
private caterers to guide the managers of these kitchens. 
3. There should be formal, approved and authenticated document, issued to 
private caterers wherein stringent standard guidelines are detailed for 
maintaining such kitchens. 
4. Lack of understanding within the staff regarding the concept of mass 
production. 
5. No food production safety norms were being observed or were even within 
the knowledge of the kitchen staff. 
6. The transfer of food from the kitchen to the pantry car was being done in 
steel containers for its final packing on the train. No awareness about 
holding temperatures was found amongst the staff. 
7. System of garbage disposal inside the kitchen is less effective. 
8. Food was not being prepared as per the standardized recipes. 
9. Regular and proper training programmes should be organized for the 
kitchen staff particularly touching the areas of hygiene, quality and 
quantity of cooking. 
10. Periodic and regular cleaning and pest control schedules must be put in 
place in the kitchens of private caterers. 
In compliance to the above observation, Indian Railway Catering and Tourism 
Corporation (IRCTC), have taken the following steps to effect impr ovement in 
Railways' catering services:- 
1. Catering licenses for five trains have been cancelled. 
2. Qualified quality control professionals have been deputed for carrying out 
the inspections of licensed catering units and accordingly advising the 
licensee for improvement and special training programme has been 
conducted for the staff of these licensed catering units. 
3. M/s. TUV has been engaged to carry out food safety audit of licensee 
managed catering units. 
4. M/s. IMRB has been engaged to conduct on -board custom er satisfaction 
survey to ascertain the overall quality of catering services.

Changes in Railways Security System 
699. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) what changes have been made in railways security system to plug loopholes 
which facilitated bomb blasts on 11th July 2006 in Mumbai suburban trains, followed by 
similar blasts on February 19th, 2007 in Samjhauta Express; 
(b) how many attacks on trains by Naxalite groups have been made in the year 
2006;and 
(c) how this vulnerability of the present railway security system is being  
adequately taken care of and what long-term measures are proposed in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI R.VELU): 
(a) In the aftermath of bomb blasts in Mumbai suburban trains and explosion in 
Samjhauta Express, following preventive measure are being taken to plug the loopholes 
in railways security system:- 
  Sniffer dogs are being utilized to check explosive m aterial in trains/ 
railway stations/railway premises. 
 Railway Protection force and Government Railway Police staff are being 
deployed for escorting of Mail/Express/Shatabdi/Rajdhani Express trains. 
 Luggage/baggage checking of passengers at entry gate, is b eing done by 
Government Railway Police/Railway Protection Force/Commercial staff at 
railway stations. 
 Intelligence staff are being geared up and instructed to maintain close 
liaison with Intelligence Bureau, special Branch and other intelligence 
agencies. 
 Regular meetings with Government Railway Police/Civil Police/ 
Intelligence Agencies are being held. 
 Joint Sammelans with Government Railway Police, Coolies, Vendors, Taxi 
drivers, Railway employees etc. are being organized. 
 The empty rake is locked at Plat form and is escorted by Railway Protection 
Force from Platform to sick/washing line. 
 Basic security arrangements are also strengthened by minimizing the entry 
points and repairing of boundary walls of station limit, yard, etc. 
 Railway Protection/Force esco rting staff are being provided in proper 
strength. 
 Frisking of all passengers and manual checking of their luggage has been 
introduced. 
 Sniffer dogs are being deployed for checking of empty rakes of the above 
trains at platforms from where the trains start. 
 Close Circuit Televisions are being installed at Important Railway Stations. 

Written answers to [17 AUG., 2007] Unstarred questions   167 
 Modern security gadgets like  Hand Held Metal Detectors, Door Frame Metal 
Detectors, X -Rays baggage scanners etc. ar e being provided at important 
stations. 
(b) (i) Attack by a group of armed Naxalites over South East Central Railway  
between Darakasa -Batalao Railway Stations of Nagpur Division in Maharashtra State  
on 06.12.2006. 
(ii) Maoist attack in trains on 15.10.2006 by about 50/60 armed Naxilites at Topadih 
Railway Station of Chakardharpur Division. They set on fire three loco engines.  
(iii)  On 10.10.2006, 25/30 armed Naxalites attacked Railway Protection Force Cash 
escorting party in train No. 346- Down Tata-Kadakpur passenger and snatched two 303 
Rifles and 30 rounds causing on duty two Railway Protection Force staff serious 
bleeding injury. 
(c) The vulnerability of the present railway security system is being taken care  
of by the following ways:- 
 By procuring Modern security gadgets. 
 By close and effective supervision of the staff. 
 By surprise done by supervisory staff in day time as well as in night. 
 By enhancing Manpower. 
 By strengthening the Dog Squad. 
In addition, to the above following long -term measures are als o under 
implementation:- 
Installation of X-Ray Screening machines and Close Circuit Televisions at important 
Railway Stations. Based on need and expert opinion, further measures will be taken in 
future.

All cases of Indian Penal Code (IPC) crimes on railways are reported to, registered 
and inv estigated by the concerned Government Railway Police (GRP) of the State 
Governments. 
(d) and (e) There is no provision in the rules for compensation for loss/theft/ damage 
of passengers' luggage/belongings unless a railway official servant has booked the 
luggage and given a receipt thereof to the passenger or unless it is proved that the loss 
was due to negligence or misconduct on the part of the railways. 
(f) According to Entry No. 2 of the State List of the Constitution of India, 'Police' 
(including Railw ays and village Police), is a State subject. The State Police has a 
separate wing called the Government Railway Police (GRP) for dealing with all matters 
relating to law and order on the Railways. Prevention and detection of crime is the 
constitutional res ponsibility of the State Governments, and as such, Ministry of 
Railways has to depend largely on them for control of crime over Railways.  
However, to effectively supplement the efforts of the State Governments in 
controlling crime on the Railways, the Railway Protection Force (RPF) staff are also 
being deployed to escort many trains and on access control duties in the passenger area 
to augment the efforts of the State Governments. The following measures have been 
taken for safety and security of the passengers:- 
1. About 2230 Trains are being escorted by Government Railway Police and 
about 1450 trains are being escorted by Railway Protection Force as on date 
in vulnerable sections. 
2. Regular announcements are being made through Public Address System as 
well as Lo ud Hailers to educate passengers regarding the menance of 
drugging and other crimes. 
3. Regular co-ordination meeting with GRP/State Police is being held to share 
intelligence regarding criminals indulging in crime against Railway 
passengers. 
4. Special squads have been constituted to tackle the menace of drugging, crime  
against women etc. in vulnerable trains and on stations.

Loco running staff 
†738. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the loco running staff has to work 12- 14 hours daily and 
as a result of which the incidents of physical and mental tension among them are 
coming to light; 
(b) whether the number of other essential staff is also being reduced; 
(c) whether this is adversely affecting the maintenance work; and 
(d) the reaction of the Government thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHIR R. VELU): 
(a) The working hours of loco running staff have been fixed as 104 hours in a two 
weekly period of 14 days including preparatory and complementary wor k. As per extant 
instructions, running duty at a stretch should not ordinarily exceed 10 hours from 
departure of the train and overall duty should not exceed 12 hours from signing on to 
signing off. Only in exceptional exigencies like accidents, floods, agitation, equipment 
failures etc. they have to work beyond duty hours stipulated in the rules. This may in 
some cases, result in longer hours of duty but all efforts are made to contain the duty 
hours within the parameters laid down and the position is cons tantly monitored at all 
levels. 
(b) to (d) No, Sir. The strength of essential safety category staff is continuously 
reviewed to ensure that safety and reliability of train operations is not compromised.

743. SHRI AMAR SINGH: SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the Minister of STEEL 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have since given its approval for the s etting up of South  
Korean Company Posco's 12 million tonnes steel project in Orissa; 
(b) if so, what are the details thereof including the proposed location of the venture 
referred to above; and 
(c) by when, it is likely to be set up? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STEEL (DR. AKHILESH DAS): 
(a) Government of Orissa has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with 
POSCO India Private Limited on 22.6.2005 for setting up a 12 million tonnes steel 
project in Orissa. 
(b) The proposed location of the steel plant is Ersama block of Jagatsinghpur district 
in Orissa. The other features of the project as per MoU are: - 
(i) The project would be implemented in two phases. Each phase will have two 
modules of 3 million tonnes per annum crude steel capacity. 
(ii) Proposed investment is of the order of around US $ 12 billion (Rs. 51,000 
crores approximately). 
(iii) POSCO will also set up infrastructure necessary for the integrated steel 
plant, related projects and related mining of iron ore and other ores. 
(iv) The acquisition of the private land will be as per the Land Acquisition Act. 
(v) For rehabilitation of displaced families, Rehabilitation and Resettlement 
Package would be implemented as per prevailing guidelines and practices. 
(vi) POSCO has a requirement of 600 million tonnes of iron ore, POSCO's 
application of mining lease would be considered as per the prescribed 
procedure.
